question.problem:
Find the $30$th percentile of the random variable $Y$ if the probability distribution function of $Y$ is given by

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-y},\, & y\ge 0, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The $100p$th percentile of a random variable $Y$ is the number ${y}_{p}$ such that

$$
P(Y\le {y}_{p})=p.
$$

In our case, we want to find the $30$th percentile, which corresponds to the decimal $p=0.3.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le {y}_{0.3}) & ={\int }_{0}^{{y}_{0.3}}{e}^{-y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{e}^{-y}{|}_{0}^{{y}_{0.3}} \\  & =1-{e}^{-{y}_{0.3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $30$th percentile is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{e}^{-{y}_{0.3}} & =0.3 \\ {e}^{-{y}_{0.3}} & =0.7 \\ {e}^{-{y}_{0.3}} & =\frac{7}{10} \\ -{y}_{0.3} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{7}{10}) \\ {y}_{0.3} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{10}{7}) \\ {y}_{0.3} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).\end{aligned}
$$
